Subject: Exhibit B consolidation: fee aggregation & fallback mechanics

Hi Elena / NovaHealth team,

Attaching our initial markup of Exhibit B (ExhibitB_redline_v1.pdf) and the updated pricing-matrix.xlsx so you have the numbers next to the language. Two items we want to align on before legal exchange:

1) Fee aggregation: are Nova's procurement and billing teams ok with a single, consolidated volume bucket across all SKUs (recommended) versus per-SKU floors? The consolidated model significantly reduces tight per-SKU floors that could trigger early true-ups.

2) Fallback / cap-floor mechanics: the current redline triggers a temporary surcharge when monthly usage exceeds the cap. We propose a 45-day true-up window and an explicit ramp (10%/30%/60%) for surcharge application to avoid a cliff. Our legal drafted language is conservative — see clause 4.2 in the attached.

Would you be open to a short call Tues morning to walk through? If helpful, Kimberly can join to speak to the proposed compromise language and Karthik can walk the numbers.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Thanks for the materials. Attaching NovaHealth legal's annotated redline (ExhibitB_redline_Nova_v1.pdf). A few quick flags from our side:

- We are generally supportive of consolidated-volume buckets but need explicit language that preserves SKU-level reporting for audit and chargeback inside our org. Can Redwood confirm you can provide SKU-level invoice detail monthly?

- Clause 4.2 (fallback surcharge): we cannot accept a staged surcharge that would retroactively apply beyond the billing period without a cap on the maximum surcharge per billing cycle. Please propose a floor/ceiling on aggregate surcharge exposure per month.

- True-up timing: Legal wants the standard 30-day true-up; procurement is willing to discuss 45 days if legal signs off.

We can do a call Tues at 10:00am ET if that works.

Regards,

Elena Rossi
Senior Counsel, Contracts | NovaHealth
elena.rossi@novahealth.com

Elena —

Appreciate the quick review and the annotated file. I pulled together a short counter-proposal and highlighted two clean edits that I think preserve both parties' protections. See attached: ExhibitB_consolidated_proposal_v2.pdf. Summary of the changes: 

1) SKU-level reporting: we will deliver a monthly invoice CSV with per-SKU usage and effective per-token rates for audit/chargeback. We'll add the reporting commitment as a new subsection under 2.1 (Reporting & Invoicing).

2) Surcharge guardrails: instead of an uncapped staged surcharge, Redwood proposes a per-cycle maximum surcharge equal to 12% of the applicable invoice period charges (cap) with the staged application you proposed (10%/30%/60%) only to determine the incremental application timing. This keeps total exposure finite and predictable. Please see proposed language in section 4.2(b).

3) True-up window: we can accept 45 days provided Nova's legal confirms the audit scope and that the parties will use the agreed invoice CSV as the baseline for any adjustments. That way both sides avoid costly re-audits.

If that sounds reasonable, Jordan will send an updated order summary and we can lock the language in before legal marking for signature. Proposed call is Tue 10:00am ET — Kimberly (legal) and Jordan (AE) on our side.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Contracts | Redwood Inference
